items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I met his drummer whose name was Kansas Field. I became better acquainted with Kansas later when he came to New York.

ctx.x: When we came off the bandstand for an intermission, Teddy told me that I should not play high notes in that place, and I replied by saying that I didn't see anything wrong with it because I made a high note, and told him that no one ever said anything to him about playing high notes on the piano. He didn't like what I had said, and never said anything about the notes I made after that.

There was a small hotel on the Southside that had a club which featured small combos and was open until the wee hours every morning. There were also musicians playing in most of the bars and Chicago was jumping. Al and I were drinking buddies and we used to go to this hotel most every night after we finished at the "Pump Room" which was at 2 a.m. The club was managed by a dancer called Broadway, whom I knew in New York. Roy Eldridge brought a band in during our stay in the city and I met his drummer whose name…

We had Monday nights off, and one Monday night, the orchestra of Count Basie played a dance at some large hall which gave me the opportunity of hearing Basie in person for the first time. When I was in Egypt, I had rented a big radio and had heard a broadcast of Basie for the first time. I had not heard of the band before but I immediately recognized Dickie Wells. But being able to hear the band and see it for the first time was real kicks and I'll never forget the impression I had listening to them.
